status.main_product: AquaVac Advanced Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (NPWT) System
status.scope_reason: The company develops, manufactures, and sells its own negative pressure wound therapy device under the brand name AquaVac Advanced.
status.evidence: According to a feature by the Department of Science and Technology, Ayo Tech Corporation developed and actively sells the AquaVac Advanced Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Device.

claims.claim: Technical specifications published by the Philippine Council for Health Research and Development (PCHRD) state that the Aquavac Advanced features automatic pressure regulation with leak detection and includes a backup battery lasting up to 12 hours in continuous mode and 24 hours in intermittent mode.

According to the 2024 DOST-PCHRD Annual Report, the company reports manufacturing and selling 20 units of the Aquavac Advanced device and completing a series of case studies to evaluate its efficacy and performance, alongside developing a Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) document.
claims.note: completing a series of case studies to evaluate its efficacy and performance, alongside developing a Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) document

claims.claim: The company provides an initial package of 10 sets of dressings and 5 sets of canisters utilizing locally-available materials as NPWT dressings bundled with the system launch in April 2024, as outlined by the Philippine Council for Health Research and Development (PCHRD).

The company's Aquavac Advanced device features automatic pressure regulation with leak detection for enhanced safety and an integrated digital display or screen, as documented by the Philippine Council for Health Research and Development (PCHRD).
claims.note: an integrated digital display or screen

claims.claim: Ayo Tech Corporation has manufactured 100 units and sold 20 units of its Aquavac Advanced NPWT device since its launch in April 2024, as recorded in a project profile by the Philippine Council for Health Research and Development (PCHRD).

A product brief by the Philippine Council for Health Research and Development (PCHRD) reports that Ayo Tech Corporation generated Php 1,000,000.00 in revenue from selling 20 units of the Aquavac Advanced NPWT system following its commercial launch in April 2024.

The Philippine Council for Health Research and Development reports that Ayo Tech Corporation has achieved Technology Readiness Level 9 and produced 100 units of its Aquavac Advanced device following its April 2024 launch.
